title: Add a Playwright smoke test
description: Browser smoke test via the Playwright MCP/CI: load the app, assert the WebGL canvas renders, open the panel, switch a preset, and move the points slider. Guards the Three.js/DOM glue that unit tests don't cover.

title: Persist scene to URL and localStorage
description: Serialize transforms + settings (numPoints, colorMode, showGuides) into the URL hash and/or localStorage so a fractal can be shared or restored on reload. Add a pure encode/decode module under src/app with unit tests.

title: Add a color-mode legend overlay
description: Show a small legend/scale for the active color mode (e.g. the height/radius gradient or the per-transform swatches) so the coloring is interpretable. Lives in the app/ui layer.

title: Keyboard shortcuts and accessibility pass
description: Keyboard control for camera/transform editing, focus management for the panel, ARIA on controls, and reduced-motion handling. The panel buttons already carry aria-labels; build on that.

title: Export the fractal as a PNG image
description: Add a button to capture the current view (renderer.domElement.toDataURL) and download it, for sharing renders. Consider a higher-resolution offscreen render.

title: Move the chaos game to a Web Worker
description: Offload runChaosGame + buildColors to a Web Worker (transferable Float32Arrays) so large point counts (up to 500k) don't block the main thread. The pure src/fractal core is already worker-friendly.

title: Add more IFS presets
description: Extend src/fractal/presets.ts with additional named systems (e.g. Barnsley-style fern, Vicsek/cross, dragon curve in 3D) plus buttons in the panel. Pure additions with unit tests for counts/shape.

title: Fractal Microscope: enter nested IFS copies with fresh local detail
description:
## Product outcome

Click a small copy inside an IFS, enter it, and repeat. A breadcrumb such as 2 / 1 / 4 explains where you are; Parent and Home make the journey reversible. Each entered copy receives a fresh rendering budget, so the user can explore its structure and save the discovery.

The signature demonstration is a journey through a Sierpinski tetrahedron and a genuinely non-flat Pentatope: the same few rules keep revealing an object at another scale. This turns self-similarity into something the user can navigate and understand.

## Current gap

Continuous zoom already preserves the focus, narrows the camera lens, and increases analytic Surface depth. Points and Solid still magnify a fixed global sample or grid (docs/architecture.md, Continuous zoom). Watch it build already explains individual map contributions. This proposal adds nested-copy selection, address history, and fresh local sampling beyond those shipped capabilities.

## Proposed first release

- Start with contractive, invertible similarity IFSs in both 3D and 4D. Show selectable child copies and their map labels; clicking an overlapping region offers its candidate copies instead of inventing a unique address.
- Entering isolates the selected copy. Keep an overview indicating its place in the parent. The UI must make isolation explicit: this view is the selected IFS image, not every overlapping branch in the same spatial region.
- Rebase computation into a local coordinate frame on each descent. Points generate a fresh cloud, Flame starts a fresh exposure, Solid rebuilds a locally resolved volume, and Surface traces the same selected copy through its existing 3D/4D route.
- Add Parent, Home, depth and scale readouts, and saved-view restoration through links, scene files and Collection. Keep source transforms editable through the normal editor.
- Classify navigation as View / Device and saving as Workflow. Points can update progressively; accumulation modes disclose that entering a copy restarts. Touch, keyboard, reduced motion and ordinary orbit/reset remain usable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A browser journey enters at least twelve levels of a half-scale fixture (4096 times accumulated scale change) in both dimensions, then returns through the same parents without drift or a blank/depleted point cloud.
2. Independently composed finite map words agree with the displayed selected copy. Asymmetric branches, overlaps and a nonzero rotated 4D slice catch wrong composition order and wrong slice handling.
3. All four render modes display the same chosen copy on supported documents; fresh Points/Flame sampling and local Solid voxelization are verified rather than inferred from a camera change. Existing Surface engine gates still apply.
4. A copied link and a saved scene restore the source document, address and local view. Editing/removing/reordering a referenced map invalidates or explicitly rebinds the path; it never silently navigates to a different copy.
5. Unsupported compositions retain their authored fields and explain the refusal beside the entry control. Plain viewing, continuous zoom, Parent and Home cannot be stranded.
6. A bounded browser qualification records visible detail, memory, latency, cancellation and numeric limits at increasing depth on real hardware. Finite precision and work limits are disclosed.
design:
The shared core should define an address as an ordered finite word and its selected set as F_word(A), with one composition-order definition consumed by the 3D and 4D affine helpers. The ordinary independent-choice chaos game admits sampling a selected word image by applying that word to fresh base samples; overlap means this is an address-selected measure, not a spatially conditioned measure.

Reuse affine.ts / affine4.ts, chaos-game.ts / chaos-game-4d.ts, orbit.ts, four-d-view.ts, the worker session protocols, existing renderers and persist.ts. Store the symbolic address and relative frame against an exact source scene; repeatedly multiplying ever-smaller world coordinates is not a deep-navigation implementation. The implementation decision must cover orientation, scale, color attribution, point size, clipping and camera-space lighting across all consumers.

In 4D, derive the current query plane and thickness through the local frame before reducing dimensions. A child rotation or translation can change the local slice; blindly taking local w = the old sliceCenter displays a different object. Pin both the flat anchor and a truly non-flat, off-centre rotated slice.

The initial similarity gate is an algebraic scope choice for stable rebasing, not a 3D-first shortcut. General affine anisotropy, nontrivial xaos, emitters, scheduled words, nonlinear maps/final lenses, tiling and balloon need explicit eligibility decisions; do not silently strip them or assume F_word(A) is the whole authored display set. Include both dimensions in every admitted case.

Effort/risk: large, including all four consumers and both dimensions. The first implementation slice should prove local sampling and 4D plane rebasing with a small CPU oracle and browser prototype before promising seamless flight. This is the recommended first bet for a distinctive IFS interaction; it can be delivered independently of the other proposals.

Mathematical reference: Hutchinson, Fractals and Self Similarity, section 3.1, establishes invariant sets and their symbolic coding. The navigation and rebasing design above is a proposed application, not a performance claim from the paper: https://maths-people.anu.edu.au/~john/Assets/Research%20Papers/fractals_self-similarity.pdf
acceptance_criteria:
1. A browser journey enters at least twelve levels of a half-scale fixture (4096 times accumulated scale change) in both dimensions, then returns through the same parents without drift or a blank/depleted point cloud.
2. Independently composed finite map words agree with the displayed selected copy. Asymmetric branches, overlaps and a nonzero rotated 4D slice catch wrong composition order and wrong slice handling.
3. All four render modes display the same chosen copy on supported documents; fresh Points/Flame sampling and local Solid voxelization are verified rather than inferred from a camera change. Existing Surface engine gates still apply.
4. A copied link and a saved scene restore the source document, address and local view. Editing/removing/reordering a referenced map invalidates or explicitly rebinds the path; it never silently navigates to a different copy.
5. Unsupported compositions retain their authored fields and explain the refusal beside the entry control. Plain viewing, continuous zoom, Parent and Home cannot be stranded.
6. A bounded browser qualification records visible detail, memory, latency, cancellation and numeric limits at increasing depth on real hardware. Finite precision and work limits are disclosed.

title: Collage Studio: fit an editable 3D/4D IFS to a target shape
description:
## Product outcome

Let the user work backwards from a shape they want. Arrange a handful of miniature copies over a target, lock the promising maps, then ask the app to improve the fit. The result is an ordinary editable IFS that can be explored, evolved, morphed and rendered.

A useful demonstration starts with a branching target, places small copies along its branches, and turns those placements into a self-similar sculpture. A companion 4D demonstration fits a target with real w extent and inspects several of its resulting slices.

## Current gap

The transform editor and Evolution Lab already support manual and selective discovery. Custom meshes already supply condensation shapes. Neither workflow seeks a small collection of recursive rules whose attractor approximates a user-selected target. The target here guides the search; the accepted result regenerates from the fitted transforms alone.

## Proposed first release

- Add a session-local Workflow workspace with Target, Collage and Generated attractor views, sharing framing and scale. Offer a frozen point sample of the current 3D or 4D scene as a target, plus bounded editable target points/strokes. Existing local mesh sampling can supply 3D targets.
- Let users place, rotate and scale a bounded number of copies of that target. Each copy is a candidate affine map. Expose exact numeric controls and locks; in 4D expose w translation/scale and the hidden rotation planes.
- Run a seeded, cancellable worker search over unlocked parameters, with progressive best-so-far previews and a visible measured fit score. Choose the map count explicitly and preserve contraction.
- Start with a compact affine domain in both dimensions. Export the accepted result through the existing scene document and normal undoable replace-load; subsequent editing, Collection, Evolution and rendering use existing paths.
- Keep the target data and optimizer state local to the workspace. Saving the fitted scene needs no target asset, backend or inference service. Any retained target-project format is a later storage decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A user can initialize a collage, improve its generated fit, lock a map, cancel a search and adopt the last accepted candidate without losing the starting scene. Adoption is one undoable action.
2. The first feasibility harness uses known 3D and non-flat 4D IFS targets, perturbed starts, and deliberately unsuitable targets. Fixed seeds reproduce the result; held-out target coverage improves over the frozen starts on the declared recoverable fixtures.
3. Every accepted map satisfies the declared full-dimensional contraction bound, including composed linear stages. Locks stay exact; a candidate cannot improve a geometric fit merely by changing point density or sampling weights.
4. Held-out generated-attractor comparisons, multiple camera directions, and several rotated/offset 4D slices verify the result. A single attractive projection or a lower collage surrogate score does not constitute success.
5. A promoted scene survives link/file/Collection round trips and regenerates after the target is removed. Points, Flame, Solid and eligible Surface routes consume that same document in both dimensions.
6. Search remains interruptible with explicit time, point-count and memory budgets. Failure to improve reports the achieved error and preserves the best candidate; no claim of exact reconstruction or general automatic recovery.
design:
Use a dimension-independent objective and optimization policy, with affine.ts / affine4.ts supplying the arithmetic. Optimize only fields that the ordinary scene codec can represent; round-trip candidates through that codec before scoring/adoption so the scored system is the system users save. Reuse seeded RNG, worker cancellation, immutable scene snapshots, exact numeric controls, the shared Surface eligibility resolver and existing target mesh sampling where applicable.

A useful starting surrogate is the discrepancy between target T and the union of its transformed copies. For genuinely contractive maps, the Collage Theorem relates exact Hausdorff collage error epsilon to attractor error at most epsilon / (1 - s). A sampled symmetric distance or multiscale coverage score is only an optimization proxy, not a certified Hausdorff bound. Retain a held-out generated-attractor score and penalize collapse, missing branches and unnecessary maps. Do not infer geometric membership from a distance-estimator threshold.

4D target points must carry real xyzw coordinates. A stroke on a posed slice must be lifted using its recorded plane; a lone 2D image or 3D projection cannot determine a unique hidden 4D shape. The first release fits explicitly supplied 4D geometry and tests native non-flat fixtures alongside the flat anchor. Later multi-view silhouette fitting needs its own identifiability decision.

Start by measuring recoverability and latency before building the full workspace. Multi-start or derivative-free local refinement is a candidate, not a settled algorithm. Measure contraction conditioning near s = 1 and distinguish target complexity limits from search failure. Benchmark the exact saved candidates in ordinary renderers, not only a private optimizer preview. If a Surface sheet is useful, reuse scripts/de-preview.ts.

Effort/risk: extra large, with the highest research uncertainty of these proposals; 3D and 4D objective, editing and qualification costs are included. The first delivery slice is a bounded feasibility study with explicit go/no-go criteria and retained manual collage authoring as the useful fallback. Broad automatic reconstruction is not a promised first release.

Reference: Hadzieva, Exact solution of an inverse problem for affine images of IFS attractors, section 1.2 / Theorem 1.5, states the Collage Theorem and distinguishes general approximate inverse fitting from the paper's much narrower exact affine-image construction. The proposed interactive optimizer is an inference from that foundation, not a claimed result of the paper: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13663-026-00834-8

2. The first feasibility harness uses known 3D and non-flat 4D IFS targets, perturbed starts, and deliberately unsuitable targets. Fixed seeds reproduce the result; held-out target coverage improves over the frozen starts on the declared recoverable fixtures.
3. Every accepted map satisfies the declared full-dimensional contraction bound, including composed linear stages. Locks stay exact; a candidate cannot improve a geometric fit merely by changing point density or sampling weights.
4. Held-out generated-attractor comparisons, multiple camera directions, and several rotated/offset 4D slices verify the result. A single attractive projection or a lower collage surrogate score does not constitute success.
5. A promoted scene survives link/file/Collection round trips and regenerates after the target is removed. Points, Flame, Solid and eligible Surface routes consume that same document in both dimensions.
6. Search remains interruptible with explicit time, point-count and memory budgets. Failure to improve reports the achieved error and preserves the best candidate; no claim of exact reconstruction or general automatic recovery.

title: 4D Slice Atlas: discover and share a family of 3D fractal cross-sections
description:
## Product outcome

Show a 4D IFS as a navigable family of 3D cross-sections. Open an atlas, compare an ordered strip of slices at once, rotate the slicing plane, pin striking views, and turn selected views into a shareable scene or a timeline sweep.

The signature demonstration is a Pentatope or Tesseract whose islands appear, split and join as the slice moves. Users can see how the different 3D objects belong to one authored 4D system while retaining the whole projected object as context.

## Current gap

W slicing, rotor controls, saved FourDPose values and timeline interpolation already exist. Four-view mode shows X/Y/Z/current camera views of one current projection. Neither provides a comparable set of different W cross-sections or a retained way to search through them. This feature organizes the existing 4D mathematics into an exploration workspace.

## Proposed first release

- Add a Slice Atlas workspace under View / Device for non-flat scenes. Show the current full projection as context and a bounded ordered strip/grid of Points previews at recorded slice centres and a shared rotor pose.
- Lock camera, framing, palette normalization and slice-width semantics across previews by default, so changing size or density remains visible. Offer explicit per-card inspection without silently auto-fitting every slice.
- Moving the atlas range or rotating its plane progressively refreshes the cards. Selecting a card applies its exact FourDPose to the main view; the active renderer produces the inspected result using its existing eligibility and settle rules.
- Pin useful poses with their source snapshot. Promote one through existing Share/Collection, or append selected poses in order to the existing Timeline with an explicit duration. Changes to the fractal cannot silently rewrite pinned discoveries.
- Keep the browsing grid and cache session-local. Portable outputs are ordinary saved views and timeline keyframes. A labelled atlas/contact-sheet export is a useful follow-on once the interactive comparison is qualified.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A user compares at least seven distinct slice positions of a genuinely non-flat IFS at once, changes the common rotor orientation, and opens any card in the main view with matching pose, framing and declared slice semantics.
2. Native Pentatope and Tesseract fixtures, an off-centre rotated fixture, and an embedded 3D anchor pin the coordinate convention. Different slices must be different samples of the same source scene, not different camera angles of one projection.
3. Cards visibly distinguish sampled Points previews from inspected Flame, Solid or analytic Surface output. Ghost context, thickness and each renderer's refusal/approximation remain clear; a sparse sampled preview never certifies an empty exact slice.
4. Pinned poses survive subsequent exploration unchanged. Share/reload and Collection restore the selected FourDPose; explicit Timeline insertion reproduces the ordered poses in playback and frame-exact export without altering transforms.
5. Rapid scrubbing, scene replacement and closing the workspace cancel obsolete jobs. A late thumbnail cannot appear under a newer pose label. Raw point buffers and thumbnail caches have explicit bounded ownership.
6. Browser qualification covers all four main render modes, real 4D rotation and offset slicing, touch/keyboard selection, reduced motion, cancellation and repeated open/close. The atlas remains reachable while costly renderer work settles.
design:
Reuse four-d-view.ts / FourDPose, project4.ts, the canonical radius normalization and slice-color definitions, scene.ts's view layout patterns, worker request generations, Collection, Timeline and existing capture readiness. Do not invent a second W normalization or reinterpret raw w as the displayed slice coordinate.

Share one bounded raw 4D Points sample per source snapshot when possible, projecting it into several lightweight cards. Label those cards as previews of finite sampling and the current soft slice. Refining an inspected card uses one normal main renderer session; do not allocate a bank of live Surface or accumulation renderers. Visible cards have priority, and invalidation keys include source scene, rotor, slice, width and relevant appearance state.

The atlas is specifically a 4D View capability: a nontrivial family of W cross-sections has no counterpart for a flat 3D scene at its default pose. Keep ordinary 3D viewing available and explain the atlas's applicability beside its entry point; do not invent w extent or change the source document to enable it. The embedded-3D anchor is the dimensional reduction oracle. There is no new 3D-only core awaiting a lift: the new work composes the already twinned renderers around genuine 4D input.

Separate comparison geometry from rendering conventions. Points and Flame retain their defined soft-slice ghost treatment; Solid and Surface use their own established slice/slab contracts and may refuse nonzero thickness. Matching card/main state means the same posed query, not a promise that those renderers produce identical silhouettes. Claims that components connect, or that a slice is empty, require stronger evidence than preview pixels.

Panel placement: atlas controls and pins are View / Device; Save, Share and Add to Timeline are Workflow actions. Opening the workspace should preserve shared accordion state. Disclose which controls update previews live, restart an accumulation on release, or await Surface settle. Honour the existing timeline cap and explicitly refuse an over-cap insertion.

Effort/risk: medium-to-large, mostly view composition, scheduling and browser qualification; includes 4D semantics, flat-scene applicability, all four inspector consumers and persistence. It can ship independently and offers the shortest route of these proposals to making the site's fourth dimension easier to understand.

Project evidence: docs/4d-exploration.md (one 4D system as a family of 3D slices), docs/architecture.md (rotor/slice lifetimes, renderer differences and saved views), and docs/panel-ia.md (control families and edit disclosure). These establish existing behavior; the atlas itself is a product proposal.

2. Native Pentatope and Tesseract fixtures, an off-centre rotated fixture, and an embedded 3D anchor pin the coordinate convention. Different slices must be different samples of the same source scene, not different camera angles of one projection.
3. Cards visibly distinguish sampled Points previews from inspected Flame, Solid or analytic Surface output. Ghost context, thickness and each renderer's refusal/approximation remain clear; a sparse sampled preview never certifies an empty exact slice.
4. Pinned poses survive subsequent exploration unchanged. Share/reload and Collection restore the selected FourDPose; explicit Timeline insertion reproduces the ordered poses in playback and frame-exact export without altering transforms.
5. Rapid scrubbing, scene replacement and closing the workspace cancel obsolete jobs. A late thumbnail cannot appear under a newer pose label. Raw point buffers and thumbnail caches have explicit bounded ownership.
6. Browser qualification covers all four main render modes, real 4D rotation and offset slicing, touch/keyboard selection, reduced motion, cancellation and repeated open/close. The atlas remains reachable while costly renderer work settles.
